title: CPR (adult)
summary: For a person who is unresponsive and not breathing normally.
steps: Check the scene is safe, then tap the person and shout to see if they respond.
Call 108 or 112, or ask someone nearby to call. Ask for an AED if one is available.
Place the heel of one hand on the centre of the chest, with the other hand on top.
Push hard and fast: about 5 to 6 cm deep, 100 to 120 compressions per minute.
Let the chest rise fully between compressions.
Continue until help arrives, an AED is ready, or the person starts to move.
warnings: If you are not trained, do hands-only CPR (compressions only).
Do not stop to check for a pulse again and again.

title: Severe bleeding
summary: Heavy bleeding that does not stop on its own.
steps: Call 108 or 112.
Press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth or bandage.
If blood soaks through, add more cloth on top. Do not remove the first layer.
Keep steady pressure and, if possible, raise the injured limb above the heart.
Keep the person lying down and warm until help arrives.
warnings: Do not remove objects stuck in the wound.
Use a tourniquet only if you are trained and pressure is not controlling life-threatening limb bleeding.

title: Burns
summary: Burns from heat, hot liquid, fire or chemicals.
steps: Move away from the source of the burn.
Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes.
Remove rings, watches and loose clothing near the burn, unless stuck to the skin.
Cover loosely with a clean, non-fluffy cloth or cling film.
Get medical help for large, deep or facial burns, and burns in children.
warnings: Do not use ice, butter, toothpaste or oil.

title: Choking (adult)
summary: A person cannot cough, speak or breathe because something blocks the airway.
steps: Ask 'Are you choking?' and encourage them to keep coughing if they can.
If they cannot breathe, give up to 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades.
If that fails, give up to 5 abdominal thrusts: fist above the navel, pull inwards and upwards.
Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts.
If the person becomes unresponsive, call 108 or 112 and start CPR.
warnings: For babies under 1 year, use back blows and chest thrusts, not abdominal thrusts.

title: Broken bone or sprain
summary: Pain, swelling or an odd shape after a fall or impact.
steps: Keep the injured part still and support it in the position found.
Pad and splint above and below the injury if you must move the person.
Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth for 15 to 20 minutes.
Check for numbness, pale or cold skin beyond the injury.
Get medical help. Call 108 for a suspected neck or back injury and do not move the person.
warnings: Do not try to straighten the bone.
Do not give food or drink if surgery may be needed.

title: Heart attack
summary: Chest pain or pressure, sweating, pain in the arm or jaw, shortness of breath.
steps: Call 108 or 112 immediately.
Help the person sit down and rest in a comfortable position.
Loosen tight clothing and keep them calm.
If the operator advises it and the person is not allergic, they may chew one adult aspirin.
If they stop breathing normally, start CPR.
warnings: Do not let the person walk or drive to hospital.

title: Snake bite
summary: A bite from a snake that may be venomous.
steps: Move away from the snake and call 108 or 112.
Keep the person calm and as still as possible.
Keep the bitten limb still and at or slightly below heart level.
Remove rings and tight items before swelling starts.
Go to a hospital quickly, even if the person feels fine.
warnings: Do not cut the wound, suck out venom or apply a tight tourniquet.
Do not try to catch the snake. A photo from a safe distance helps.
